name: DB4IoT
tagline: Moonshadow Mobile's hosted geospatial time-series engine for connected-vehicle analytics; offline since 2025.
description: DB4IoT was a cloud-hosted database engine and analytics platform from Moonshadow Mobile in Oregon, built for the 'internet of moving things': billions of timestamped location points from connected vehicles, transit fleets and phones. It stored this data in a compact columnar format and served interactive, map-based queries, letting transportation planners draw polygons, build origin-destination matrices, trace routes through ordered pass-through filters and compare corridors in seconds, with packaged offerings on INRIX Trips and Wejo connected-vehicle data. By 2021 it was marketed mainly as a mobility analytics product rather than a general database. The db4iot.com site went offline in 2025, and Moonshadow now promotes engineering services and its Ephemeris datastore technology instead.
statusNote: db4iot.com went offline in 2025 and Moonshadow Mobile no longer markets the product; it now offers engineering services and its Ephemeris datastore.

scale.notes: Hosted service handling large connected-vehicle trip datasets; architecture details were not published.

strengths: Interactive origin-destination and route analysis over very large trip datasets
Compact columnar storage tuned for location time series
Packaged integrations with INRIX Trips and Wejo connected-vehicle data
weaknesses: No longer offered; the product site is offline
Proprietary hosted service with no self-managed option
useCases: Historical reference for mobility analytics platforms
Understanding legacy transportation-planning workflows built on it
